symptom: `revoke write (NewAttr) on entity M.E from M.RoleA, M.RoleB, M.RoleC` printed "Unchanged entity access: M.E (M.RoleA, M.RoleB, M.RoleC) — nothing to revoke", exited 0, and `show access` still listed NewAttr: ReadWrite in each rule; check and mxbuild clean (mendixlabs/mxcli#1501).
cause: The rules were granted one role each, so each stored a single-role ModuleRoles list. RevokeEntityMemberAccess only narrowed a rule whose role set EQUALLED the statement's ({A,B,C}); none did, 0 rules modified, reported as already revoked. RemoveEntityAccessRule (full revoke) had always matched per role, so only the partial form was affected.
file: mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel_security_write.go (RevokeEntityMemberAccess: narrow every rule all of whose roles are named; refuse, before writing, a rule shared with an unnamed role)
insight: The reporter's hypothesis (write comes from the rule's default member access, no stored entry to narrow) was wrong, and one control settled it: the same revoke naming ONE role narrowed NewAttr on the same project, so the entries existed. When a report pins a multi-target statement, re-run it with a single target before reading the member logic — the variable that changed was the role list, not the member. Grant keys a rule on its exact role set (+ XPath) because that is identity for an upsert; revoke is a filter, and copying grant's key into it made a three-role statement match nothing. A rule shared with a role the statement does not name must be refused, not narrowed: narrowing it would silently revoke the unnamed role's right too. Measured on pedapp (11.13): old binary prints the Unchanged notice with ReadWrite x3; fixed binary narrows all three to ReadOnly, a rerun prints the honest Unchanged notice, and `mx check` reports the same 1002 pre-existing fixture errors as the unfixed copy, none on the entity.
